segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive a vehicle
over any bridge or other elevated structure constituting a part of a highway
at a speed which is greater than the maximum speed which can be maintained with safety to the bridge or structure,
when such structure is signposted as provided in this section

The Department of Transportation upon request from any local authority shall, or upon its own initiative may, conduct an investigation of any bridge or other elevated structure constituting a part of a highway constructed and maintained under the authority granted by chapter 408 of NRS,
and if it thereupon finds that such structure cannot with safety to itself withstand vehicles traveling at the speed otherwise permissible under chapters 484A to 484E, inclusive, of NRS,
the Department shall determine and declare the maximum speed of vehicles which such structure can safely withstand,
and shall cause or permit suitable signs stating such maximum speed to be erected and maintained
at a distance of 100 feet before each end of such structure.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'any person to drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Driving over a bridge or other elevated structure: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.elevated_structure, 'bridge, viaduct or tunnel carrying the roadway', that lies on a highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway) — the structure 'constituting a part of a highway'.

The maximum speed which can be maintained with safety to the structure is the one the sign states: the value of a dev.speed_limit_sign of kind structure_maximum ('sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit') governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) while on the structure; greater than is kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') above that value. The safety of the structure is the authority's determination (y8), not a judgement left to the driver, so the span is no standard.

Signposted: a dev.speed_limit_sign of kind structure_maximum governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) while on the structure; 'as provided in this section' is read from the sign's presence (observable_reading status). dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position', so the sign's distance from the structure is not read from it.

The suitable signs stating such maximum speed are dev.speed_limit_sign of kind structure_maximum, whose value is the declared maximum; their erection and maintenance are read from their presence and governance (dev.governs) of the structure's travel regions.

residues.why: The authority's investigation, on request or on its own initiative, of structures built under chapter 408 of NRS (outside the corpus) is the process behind the posting; the rule reads the posted sign as the evidence of it.

The authority's finding that the structure cannot withstand the otherwise permissible speeds (chapters 484A to 484E, no node of the corpus) is the reason for the posting; the rule reads the posted maximum, not the finding.
The authority's determination and declaration of the maximum speed is read through the value the posted sign states; the act of declaring is not observable.

The sign's placement before each end of the structure is the authority's duty; the rule reads the sign's governance of the structure's travel regions, not its distance from the ends, so the placement is not checked.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) occupying an elevated structure that lies on a highway, and a speed limit sign of kind structure_maximum governs a travel region the subject occupies.
obligation: Re-binding every speed limit sign of kind structure_maximum governing a travel region the subject occupies while it occupies an elevated structure on a highway, the subject's speed is at or below that sign's value. Otherwise violated.

narrowings.why: 'any person to drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

'signposted as provided in this section' is read from the presence of a structure-maximum speed sign governing the travel region the subject occupies on the structure; the authority's investigation, declaration and placement are presumed from it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A truck occupies a bridge lying on a highway; a structure_maximum speed sign of 11 m/s governs the bridge lane it occupies; its speed is 16 m/s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same truck on the same bridge at 10 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car on a bridge lying on a highway whose lanes no structure_maximum speed sign governs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe which regions the speed limit sign governs, so whether the bridge is signposted is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car at 16 m/s on an ordinary roadway lane, off any elevated structure, though a structure_maximum sign governs the lane ahead of the bridge.
